editorial:
Imagine taking a boring subject like sidewalk cement and trying to turn it into a cheesy romance movie. That is exactly what happens here. You follow John Wilson, a quirky filmmaker who goes to a class on how to write Hallmark movies. Instead of making a story about a big-city girl moving to a small town, he decides to use those same emotional tricks to make a movie about concrete. It is a weird, funny, and totally random ride that makes you laugh at how silly movie formulas actually are. You will feel like you are just hanging out with a funny friend who is obsessed with the most boring things in the world.

The best part is how the movie mixes real-life footage with these dramatic, fake movie tropes. The pacing is great because it never feels too slow, even when talking about rocks and water. One downside is that it might feel too random for some people, but that is part of the charm. If you love dry humor, you need to see this.
endingExplained: At the very end, John tries to pitch his finished concrete movie to a big studio. In a funny twist, the executives actually love it, but not for the reasons he thinks. They think it is a satire about the housing market rather than a romance about cement. He realizes that no matter how hard he tries to follow a formula, people will always see things their own way. He ends up happy just being weird.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dry humor and weird documentaries.
